BONE-01.test: model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.add child, sibling, from mesh, new skeleton; refusals
BONE-01.note: SOEdit is wrong here: its Insert (OnBoneInsert) only calls OnBoneAdd, so it adds a child, not a sibling. Here Insert really adds the bone right after the picked one under the same parent. Names bone0, bone1, ... as in SOEdit (basis when the model has no skeleton; a new skeleton block is made then).

BONE-02.where: tools/lib/model/edit/tree.js:197 bone.add {parent}; tools/gui/ext/models/sub/tree.client.js:78 ACTS addChild (toolbar and menu)
BONE-02.test: model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.add child, sibling, from mesh, new skeleton; refusals; tree.test.js: ok 6 toolbar adds a bone
BONE-02.note: Optional name, mesh (name taken from the mesh file as SOEdit does), joint type and position or matrix. The new bone is picked and its branch opened.

BONE-03.test: model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.delete branch with volumes; refusing the root; edit-tree: bone.delete keeping children and moving volumes keeps world places; tree.test.js: ok 7
BONE-03.note: Asks first. SOEdit always deletes the whole branch and asks only about volumes; here the user can also delete the bone alone, its children move up one level and keep their place in the world (child matrix times the deleted bone's). Volumes on the deleted bones: remove, move to the parent (keeping their world place) or keep tied to no bone. Meshes go with their bone (the .ply files stay). The only root bone cannot be deleted.

BONE-04.where: tools/gui/ext/models/sub/tree.client.js:78 ACTS parent and the form button (pick the parent); tools/lib/model/edit/tree.js:330 bone.move (a real move)
BONE-04.test: tree.test.js: ok 5 left goes to the parent; model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.move keeps the world place; cycles refused; tree.test.js: ok 7 drag and drop moves a bone
BONE-04.note: In SOEdit this menu entry only picks the parent bone; that is kept. Moving a bone to another parent, which SOEdit cannot do, is added: drag a row onto another, or Move under in the form, keeping its place in the world by default. Moving a bone into itself or its own children, and the only root under a bone, are refused. Move up and Move down change the order among siblings.

BONE-05.test: tree.test.js: ok 4 the form of the picked bone; model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.get (local, world, Euler, metres, joint fields)
BONE-05.note: A form beside the tree instead of a dialog. Each change is its own edit with its own undo step.

BONE-06.test: model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: bone.rename follows volumes and animations, lists .def mentions; tree.test.js: ok 6
BONE-06.note: Better than SOEdit: volume Bone references follow, and the bone name in the document's .anm files is renamed too (can be turned off). Lines in the unit's .def files that quote the old name are listed for the user to change. Names with quotes, braces, slashes, non ASCII or a dot (a dot makes the game load a prefab) and names already used are refused.

BONE-08.test: model-edit-tree.test.js: edit-tree: setMatrix local/world, place, nudge, round, mirror; tree.test.js: ok 6 place with 2,5
BONE-08.note: 12 cells as in SOEdit (decimal comma read as a dot), plus position in units with metres shown (20 units = 1 m), angles in degrees and scale, each in the parent's space or the model's (world) space. The numbers are written back in the form the file already uses (Position, Orientation or Matrix34), changing only the numbers that differ; SOEdit rewrites the whole file.
